= update-versions

Changes the versions of a Gradle version catalog (`gradle/libs.versions.toml`) in a git repository, with *one commit for each*. It knows nothing about the release train, or where the versions come from: it is given the names and the new versions. (`map-train-versions` works them out, and `ensure-dependency-issues` has the issues.)

== What it does

For every version, in the order of the names, it changes the line `name = "value"` of the `[versions]` section of the catalog and commits it:

----
Update spring-framework to 7.0.10

Closes gh-123

Signed-off-by: github-actions[bot] <41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>
----

* *Only that line changes.* The other lines, the comments, the spaces around the equals sign and the line endings stay the way they were. A line of another section that looks the same (a library of the same name) is not touched.
* *The message is fixed.* It is not an input, so the history of a catalog reads the same everywhere. The `Closes` line is only there if the update has an issue.
* *The commit is signed off* with the identity that git is set up with (`git config user.name` and `user.email`). That is the identity of the commits, too, and it is not signed with a key.
* *Everything is checked before the first commit.* A name that is not in the catalog, a version that cannot be written, or an issue that is missing or is not a number, fails before anything is committed, so a failure does not leave some of the updates done.
* *A version that has the new value already is left alone,* with no empty commit.
* *The catalog must have no uncommitted changes.* The commit would take them with it.

== Inputs

[cols="2,1,4"]
|===
| Input | Default | Description

| `versions`
| required
| A JSON object from the name of a version to its new version: `{"spring-framework":"7.0.10"}`, or with the issue that the commit closes: `{"spring-framework":{"version":"7.0.10","issue":123}}`. The output `versions` of `map-train-versions` is the first form.

| `toml-path`
| `gradle/libs.versions.toml`
| The version catalog, in the repository.

| `path`
| `.`
| The directory of the git repository.

| `require-issue`
| `true`
| Whether every update must have an issue. Set it to `false` for updates that have none: their commits have no `Closes` line.
|===

== Outputs

[cols="1,4"]
|===
| Output | Description

| `commits`
| The commits that were made, as a JSON array of `{ dependency, version, issue, commit }`.

| `count`
| How many.
|===

== Fails when

* the input is not a JSON object, or an update has no version, or the version is not one that can be written (only letters, digits, dots, hyphens and plus signs)
* an update has no issue, and `require-issue` is `true`, or the issue is not a number
* the catalog does not exist, has no such version, or has changes that are not committed
* git cannot commit, most of all because it does not know who you are

== Secrets and permissions

None, it only works in the directory of the repository. The commits need no token. A job that goes on to push them has to be given the permission to: the release workflow pushes with the secret `RELEASE_AUTOMATION_TOKEN`, see `.github/RELEASE_AUTOMATION.adoc`.

== Using it

[source,yaml]
----
- run: |
    git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
    git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
- uses: ./.github/actions/update-versions
  with:
    versions: '{"spring-framework":{"version":"7.0.10","issue":123},"micrometer":{"version":"1.16.8","issue":124}}'
----

== Running it locally

It is an ordinary Node program (Node 24). `npm install` once in `.github/actions/`. Try it in a copy of your repository, as it makes commits:

[source,shell]
----
cd .github/actions
npm install
git clone ../.. /tmp/try-update && git -C /tmp/try-update config user.name Alice && git -C /tmp/try-update config user.email alice@example.com
export GITHUB_OUTPUT=$(mktemp)
env 'INPUT_VERSIONS={"spring-framework":{"version":"7.0.10","issue":123},"micrometer":"1.16.8"}' \
    'INPUT_REQUIRE-ISSUE=false' 'INPUT_PATH=/tmp/try-update' \
    node src/update-versions/index.js
git -C /tmp/try-update log --format='%an: %B' -3
----

`npm test` runs its tests, which make commits in temporary repositories. They need no network and no token.
